newsitem.title: USA: Reader's Digest boss leaves amid condensed earnings.
newsitem.headline: Reader's Digest boss leaves amid condensed earnings.

text.p: One month after slashing its dividend and earnings forecast, publisher Reader's Digest Association Inc. said Monday its chairman and chief executive officer, James Schadt, had resigned.
The company, renowned for its condensed-version books and monthly magazine, gave no reason for Schadt's resignation and a spokeswoman was not immediately available to comment.

Former Chief Executive Officer and Chairman George Grune, who is 68, will act as chairman and CEO, effective immediately, while a committee comprised of independent directors searches for a permanent successor to the 59-year-old Schadt, it said.
Grune led Reader's Digest's move from a private to a publicly held company, and the firm said its revenues doubled and operating profit increased ninefold during his decade at the company's helm.
Reader's Digest stock gained $2.875 to $27.75 in morning trading on the New York Stock Exchange after the announcement.
A month ago, the company halved its quarterly dividend to 22.5 cents from 45 cents per share, saying it expected disappointing earnings of $1.20 per share for the fiscal year ended June 30.

At that time the company also said it would incur fourth-quarter charges of between 20 cents and 25 cents a share to cover unwanted inventory, for which it blamed poor customer response to its third- and fourth-quarter promotional mailings.
In April, Reader's Digest reported that its earnings fell 31 percent to $37.6 million, or 35 cents a share, in the third quarter ending March 31.
At that time, the company announced a four-year $400 million programme to aggressively promote its products.
It said the board committee that will seek out Schadt's replacement will be led by James Preston, chairman and CEO of Avon Products Inc.
The committee will include Walter Shipley, chairman and CEO of Chase Manhattan Corp., and Willliam White, chairman of Bell & Howell Co.
